question: My daughter is starting at Ramapo this fall and is interested in nursing. Does Ramapo offer a nursing major for incoming freshmen, and is it a direct-admit program or does she have to apply separately after her first year?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists a Nursing Generic BSN, the generic track for students interested in becoming nurses. The curriculum has students complete general education and science requirements in the first two years; upon satisfactory completion of those courses, they enter the nursing sequence, which is two years long. [2]

The page does not say whether students are admitted directly to the major as freshmen or must submit a separate application after the first year. For clarification, contact the Nursing Programs Office at (201) 684-7749, or the School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office at SNHOffice@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7734. [2]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG)

question: How many total credits does a student need to graduate with a bachelor's degree from Ramapo?
answer:
A bachelor's degree requires at least 128 credits that count toward graduation [11]. The Registrar also states that 128 credits are required overall [5, 6], and the Center for Student Success says students need a minimum of 128 graduation credits [15]. Specific programs may require more [11].

Other requirements include at least 32 credits at Ramapo [5, 7, 11], at least 48 credits at Ramapo with the final 32 in residence [6, 8], and at least half the credits for each major, second major, or minor completed at Ramapo [6, 8]. The pages differ on the minimum credits at Ramapo: sections 5, 7, and 11 say 32, while sections 6 and 8 say 48 [5, 6, 7, 8, 11].

Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7695; D-224 [5, 6, 7, 8].

Sources: [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/)

question: Could you explain what the general education requirements are at Ramapo? I'd like to know which categories my son has to complete and roughly how many credits they add up to.
answer:
Ramapo’s General Education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses, four keystone-category courses, and courses in two of the three distribution categories [8]. The four keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits [8]. The four keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must also be completed within the first 64 credits [8]. All students must complete reading, writing, and mathematics requirements by 64 credits [10, 11].

For distribution categories, the Provost page lists Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics, and says at least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing the student’s major [8]. Another page, for changes taking effect Fall 2026, lists Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, and says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; the pages differ [9].

The curriculum should not exceed 41 credits [7]. The pages do not give an exact credit total for these ten courses [7, 8]. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements [5].

The Office of the Provost provides the General Education information: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [6].

Sources: [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: What courses should a freshman majoring in biology take in the first semester, and is there a recommended four-year plan we can look at?
answer:
The published plan is specifically “Biology: Ramapo/NYCPM 3+4 Podiatry — Fall 2026,” not a general Biology major plan. It applies to students admitted into the major during the 2026-2027 academic year. [1]
For that track, First Year, Fall (18 credits): BIOL 111 & BIOL 111L (4); CHEM 116 & CHEM 116L (4); CRWT 102 (4); INTD 101 (4). [1] The plan continues: First Year, Spring (18 credits): BIOL 113 & BIOL 113L (4); CHEM 117 & CHEM 117L (4); MATH 121 or MATH 110 (4); General Education Requirement (4); PATH 001. Second Year, Fall (18.5 credits): BIOL 332 & BIOL 332L (4); CHEM 211 & CHEM 211L (4); two General Education Requirements (4 each); PATH 002. Second Year, Spring: BIOL 221 (4); CHEM 213 & CHEM 213L (4); Biology Elective; General Education Requirement (4); PATH 003. Third Year, Fall (18.5 credits): PSYC 242 or ENSC 345 (4); PHYS 111 & PHYS 118L (4); BIOL 407 & BIOL 407L (4); General Education Requirement (4). Third Year, Spring (17 credits): CHEM 425 (4); PHYS 113 & PHYS 119L (4); BIOL 356 (4); General Education Requirement (4). Total credits required: 128 (actual RCNJ credits = 111.5). [1]
For first-year students, Center for Student Success advisors provide advising; first-semester courses are based on the declared major. Recommended Graduation Plans can help with planning. [2][3][4] Contact Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441. [2][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/)

question: Is there a first year seminar that all freshmen are required to take? What is it and how many credits is it?
answer:
Yes. The First-Year Seminar (FYS) is a general education requirement for first-year students and must be taken during the fall semester of their first year [2]. FYS is INTD 101 FIRST YEAR SEMINAR, worth 4 credits [1]. FYS courses are open only to first-semester, first-year students [3].

question: My son wants to major in computer science. What are the prerequisites for CMPS 147, and does he need to take a math placement test before he can register for it?
answer:
CMPS 147 is a required course in the Computer Science BS. [1] It is 4 credits. [3] Its prerequisite is either completing one of these courses: MATH 021 PREPARATION FOR COLLEGE MATHEMATICS PROGRAM; MATH 022 TRANSITIONAL MATHEMATICS; MATH 024 ELEMENTARY ALGEBRA TOPICS; MATH 100T TRANSFER GE MATH EQUIVALENT; MATH 101 MATH WITH APPLICATIONS; MATH 104 MATH FOR THE MODERN WORLD; MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; MATH 110 PRECALCULUS; or MATH 121 CALCULUS I; or completing one placement test with the required minimum score: ACCUPLACER Quantitative Reasoning (258), ACCUPLACER Advanced Algebra and Functions (260), ACT Composite (26), or SAT MATH (580). [3]
The course prerequisite page permits either course completion or a qualifying test score; it does not say a separate math placement test is required specifically before registering for CMPS 147. [3] However, Computer Science majors are required to take the Calculus Placement Test, even if exempt from the Math Placement Test; the stated exemption is college-level Pre-Calc or Calculus credit. [8] A separate page says SAT-Math 580 or higher places a student in a 100-level math course, and SAT/ACT scores do not exempt students from the Calculus Placement Test if calculus is required for the major. [7] It also says students intending to take MATH 110, MATH 121 or MATH 237 must take the Calculus Placement Test before registering for those courses. [10]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/math-placement/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/math-faq/) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#basic-skills-placement-testing-exemption1)

question: If my son takes Intro to Psychology (PSYC 101), will that count toward his gen ed requirements as well as toward a psychology major?
answer:

question: Is it possible to double major at Ramapo, and would a student still be able to graduate in four years if they do? For example, communication arts and psychology.
answer:
Yes. Ramapo’s guidance discusses double majoring, and its undergraduate rule for two majors says no more than half the courses may count toward both majors; all writing-intensive courses required for the second major must also be completed. [6] The Center for Student Success recommends using the Graduation Plans to assess whether you can double major. [9]

For your example, Communication Arts BA and Psychology BA are listed programs. [1][2] Each has a separate recommended four-year plan for students admitted during 2026–2027, with 128 credits required. [1][2] The pages do not establish that completing both majors together will fit into four years; the two separate plans aren’t a combined plan. The College advises declaring a major during sophomore year if you intend to graduate in four years, and notes most majors require at least two years to complete. [8]

Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) to discuss your course plan: success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. [8][9][11] Graduation Plans: https://www.ramapo.edu/mygraduationplan/ [9]

question: What does the College English / writing requirement look like for freshmen? Is there a required composition course, and what is its course number?
answer:
For first-year students, required courses depend on placement: incoming first-year students are prepackaged into appropriate courses as available. Students needing developmental reading/writing should take CRWT 080 or 090, CRWT 101, and/or developmental math in their first semester. These requirements should be completed by 64 credits; Banner blocks registration until the required courses are scheduled, and continues blocking until Critical Reading and Writing II and general education mathematics are successfully completed. [7][8]
The required General Education Critical Reading & Writing course is CRWT 102. [10] Placement information includes CRWT 101 as the first credit-bearing course in the progression, CRWT 101S with an extra weekly support class, and CRWT 102. An SAT-Evidence-Based Reading & Writing score of 620 or higher places students in CRWT 102. [10][11]

Sources: [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/post-testing/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/reading-placement/)

question: My son is undecided. In your opinion, should he major in economics or finance if he wants a good job after graduating?
answer:
I don’t have a verified opinion or information showing which major leads to better job prospects. Ramapo’s Finance description says it prepares students for careers in financial analysis, stock brokerage, money management, real estate analysis, banking, insurance and risk management, and international finance [1]. The Economics description explains the field’s focus on economic topics, but doesn’t compare job outcomes with Finance [2].

Ramapo advises that “majors don’t get you a job. Job experience does” and recommends co-op or internship experience before graduation [3,4]. Internships and research experiences increase the likelihood of working in a field related to a degree [7]. He could explore career options and labor-market trends through O*NET [8], or use FOCUS 2 to explore careers and majors (access code: ramapo430) [9].

For an undecided student, the Center for Student Success advises first-year and undeclared students through the Ramapo Exploration Program (REP) [5]. It also recommends gathering information, considering interests and strengths, and talking with faculty and advisors [4]. Contact the Center for Student Success at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 [5].

The Cahill Career Development Center recommends visiting a Career Advisor [6]. Contact careercenter@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7444 [6].

question: Does Ramapo offer a major in environmental science, and if so, what are the core courses required and how many credits is the major itself?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers Environmental Science, B.S., in the School of Science, Nursing, and Health. An Environmental Science minor is also listed. [1] [4]

Core requirements (all required):
• 100-level: BIOL 111 and 111L; CHEM 117 and 117L; ENSC 103; GEOL 106 and 106L. [1]
• 200-level: ENSC 225, ENSC 230, BIOL 221. [1]
• 300-level: BIOL 315, ENSC 303, ENSC 343 and 343L, ENSC 345, GEOL 328 and 328L. [1]
• 400-level: ENSC 417 and 417L. [1]
• Also required: 2 elective courses chosen from BIOL 320; ENSC 305, 320, 350, 390, 495; GEOL 327, 333; and PATH 001, 002, 003. [1]

The pages provided do not state the exact credit total for this major. The catalog says undergraduate majors must total at least 40 and no more than 64 credits. [8] The 128-credit figure is the total for the degree, not the major. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-ENSC) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/sustainability/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)
